name: Panels
describe: Panels over the game: a shop, an inventory (bar or grid), choice cards, a dialogue and a text field; they show and return a choice, and never pause the round
examples: a shop where coins buy upgrades
an inventory of items to use

kinds.description: Which panels this game uses: their words become slots (choice, shop, inventory, dialogue, input)

slots.dynamic: more slots follow from params (slotsFor in the implementation): one per table row or per configured kind

host.how: a panel is local to the copy that opens it (or the `for` player's copy); sending the answer to the host is the game's message

lines: A panel only shows and returns a choice: prices, money, stock and what a purchase does are rules.js. Open one on every copy that should see it; `for: player.id` makes it open on that player's copy only.
A panel never pauses the round (a live round never does); a modal one takes only your own input. Pictures are slot ids (panel.image.<file under assets/panels/>), words are the part's params.

Open: panels.shop({ items, currency, onChoose }), choice({ cards, onPick }), inventory({ items }), dialogue({ speaker, lines, choices }), input({ title, maxLength }); `h.update({ items })` after a purchase, `h.done` is a promise.

stub.worked: const shop = panels.shop({ items: [{ id: 'speed', name: 'Faster shoes', price: 10 }], currency: { label: 'Coins', amount: 0 }, onChoose: ({ id }) => { buy(id); shop.update({ currency: { label: 'Coins', amount: coins } }); } });
traps: a purchase is the game's: check the money on the host, take it, give the item, then h.update({ items, currency }) so the panel shows the new state
a panel is local: to show every player a choice call it on every copy; to answer the host send a message (ctx.net.send) from onPick/onChoose

signs: reported: its sign of life is reported, not judged
